title: CONNECT-IP HTTP Datagram Payload Architecture
purpose: Define RFC 9484 IP Proxying HTTP Datagram Context ID layout, Context ID allocation policy, Context ID zero IP packet semantics, unknown Context ID handling, and optimistic client send policy.
design_summary: `Http3ConnectIpDatagram` creates, parses, and embeds IP Proxying HTTP Datagram payloads, enforcing 62-bit variable-length Context IDs and Context ID zero full IPv4/IPv6 packet validation. `Http3ConnectIpContextIdRegistry` owns per-request dynamic non-zero allocation and reallocation rejection. `Http3ConnectIpDatagramPolicy` owns unknown Context ID handling, future extension registration recognition, payload semantics lookup, and HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 optimistic client send permission.
data_and_state_considerations: The datagram codec is stateless. Context ID allocation state is intentionally per request namespace and accepts caller-driven allocation order.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Context ID zero is reserved for complete IP packets and rejects malformed or truncated IPv4/IPv6 packets.
Nonzero Context IDs are dynamically allocated and may carry extension-defined payloads.
Unknown Context IDs are either dropped silently or buffered temporarily while awaiting registration.
risks: Forwarding, route-table selection, hop-count updates, and ICMP error generation remain separate RFC 9484 slices.
Live tunnel integration remains adapter work.
